clue.text: Writings during time back on the Isle of Man

indicators.note: during says the writings sit inside the other piece, in the middle of it
back says the word for time is read from right to left

parts.note: a year is a period of time
MS is the abbreviation for manuscript, a piece of writing

explanation.surface: A scholar's notes, composed long ago, are found again on the Isle of Man.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Writings' is plural but MS serves as the abbreviation; 'back' turns the year round and 'during' places MS in its middle, giving RAEY split by MS.
explanation.definitionFit: Ramsey is a town on the north-east coast of the Isle of Man, the self-governing island in the Irish Sea.

clue.text: River with carp. Not wide river

indicators.note: Not says the letter for wide is taken away from the complaining word

parts.note: to carp is to complain, or whine
W is the abbreviation for wide, as in cricket scoring

explanation.surface: An angler describes a waterway stocked with carp but too narrow to be called wide.
explanation.walkthrough: 'carp' looks like the fish but is the verb meaning to grumble; 'Not' removes W from WHINE to leave HINE.
explanation.definitionFit: The Rhine is a major European waterway flowing from the Alps to the North Sea.

clue.text: Sicilian port confused cyclically

indicators.note: cyclically says letters are moved round from the front of the phrase to its back

parts.note: someone confused is in a mess

explanation.surface: Someone is bewildered while sailing round a Sicilian harbour.
explanation.walkthrough: IN A MESS has its first three letters, INA, carried round to the end.
explanation.definitionFit: Messina is a port city in north-east Sicily, on the strait facing mainland Italy.

clue.text: Topless beauties — nothing better — in Shropshire

indicators.note: Topless says the first letter is cut from the word for beauties

parts.note: belles are beautiful women
mere means nothing more or better than, as in a mere child

explanation.surface: A racy tabloid boast that topless models in Shropshire cannot be bettered.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Topless' cuts B from BELLES, leaving ELLES.
explanation.definitionFit: Ellesmere is a market town in north Shropshire, known for its lakes.

clue.text: Painting by cooker top in Tasmania

indicators.note: by means placed beside, so one piece comes next to the other

parts.note: a hob is the top of a cooker where pans are heated
painting is a form of art

explanation.surface: A picture hangs beside the stove in a Tasmanian kitchen.
explanation.definitionFit: Hobart is the capital city of Tasmania, the Australian island state.

clue.text: Cosh carried regularly at US airport

indicators.note: regularly says every other letter of the two words is taken

explanation.surface: A weapon is smuggled through security at an American airport.
explanation.definitionFit: O'Hare is Chicago's main international airport.

clue.text: Giant turning up gold on WI island

indicators.note: turning says the letters of the big word are rearranged
up in a down clue says the symbol is read bottom to top

parts.note: AU is the chemical symbol for gold

explanation.surface: A giant digs up gold on a Caribbean island.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turning' rearranges GIANT into ANTIG; 'up' turns AU into UA. WI stands for the West Indies.
explanation.definitionFit: Antigua is an island in the Caribbean, part of the West Indies.

clue.text: Medway town or public school that's not taken up card game

indicators.note: taken up in a down clue says the little word is read bottom to top

parts.note: bridge is a card game for four players

explanation.surface: A pupil at a posh school refuses to join in at cards.
explanation.walkthrough: 'taken up' turns NOT into TON. A public school in Britain is a fee-paying private school; Tonbridge School is one. The Medway is a river in Kent.
explanation.definitionFit: Tonbridge is a Kent town on the River Medway and home of a well-known independent boys' school.

clue.text: Relations' drink in County Cork

parts.note: relations are kin; the possessive gives KIN'S
ale is a drink, a kind of beer

explanation.surface: A family's pint of beer in an Irish pub.
explanation.definitionFit: Kinsale is a historic harbour town on the south coast of County Cork in Ireland.

clue.text: Beheaded creature's death in Spitalfelds and Whitechapel, say

indicators.note: Beheaded says the first letter is cut off the animal word

parts.note: a beast is a creature
an end is a death, as in met his end

explanation.surface: A grisly Victorian murder of an animal in the old streets of London.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Beheaded' takes B from BEAST, leaving EAST. Spitalfields and Whitechapel are districts of the East End of London.
explanation.definitionFit: Spitalfields and Whitechapel are examples of districts in London's East End.

clue.text: Everyone agreed changing places with an artist in Eire peninsula

indicators.note: changing places says the two halves of the phrase swap round

parts.note: nem con, short for nemine contradicente, means with no one disagreeing
an gives the letter A
RA is a Royal Academician, an artist

explanation.surface: A unanimous vote to swap seats with a painter on an Irish coast.
explanation.walkthrough: 'changing places' swaps NEM CON into CONNEM. Eire is Ireland.
explanation.definitionFit: Connemara is a region of western Ireland on the Atlantic, much of it a peninsula.

clue.text: Cat by public school in Suffolk port

indicators.note: by means placed beside, so one piece follows the other

parts.note: Felix is a famous cartoon cat
Stowe is a well-known English public school

explanation.surface: A cat is found beside a posh school in a Suffolk harbour town.
explanation.walkthrough: A British public school is a fee-paying private school; Stowe is one in Buckinghamshire.
explanation.definitionFit: Felixstowe is a town in Suffolk with Britain's busiest container port.

clue.text: Hangers-on disclose French département

indicators.note: disclose says the answer is revealed inside the hyphenated word

explanation.surface: Parasites at court reveal secrets about a region of France.
explanation.definitionFit: Gers is a département in south-west France, in the Gascony region.

clue.text: Flower having faded petal

indicators.note: faded suggests the letters are worn and jumbled into a new order

explanation.surface: A bloom whose petals have withered.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Flower' looks like a bloom, but it is a crossword thing that flows, a river: the River Plate in South America.
explanation.definitionFit: Crossword convention: a flower is something that flows, a river, and the Plate is the great estuary river between Argentina and Uruguay.

clue.text: Penalties converted in the eastern Mediterranean

indicators.note: converted says the letters are changed into a new arrangement

explanation.surface: Football spot-kicks scored in a match in the Middle East.
explanation.walkthrough: 'converted' looks like scoring penalty kicks, but it signals the rearrangement.
explanation.definitionFit: Palestine is the historic region on the eastern shore of the Mediterranean.

clue.text: Two little boys in French province

parts.note: Norm is a short form of Norman, a boy's name
Andy is a short form of Andrew, a boy's name

explanation.surface: A couple of small children are found in a region of France.
explanation.definitionFit: Normandy is a historic region of northern France on the Channel coast.

clue.text: Master of Thornfield Hall disturbs the scorer in Medway town

indicators.note: disturbs says the letters are thrown into a new order

explanation.surface: The brooding hero of Jane Eyre bothers the cricket scorer in a Kent town.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Master of Thornfield Hall' is a further definition: Mr Rochester in Charlotte Brontë's Jane Eyre. The Medway is a river in Kent.
explanation.definitionFit: Rochester is a cathedral city in Kent on the River Medway.

clue.text: Palace spaniel that few during WW2

definitions.meaning: a stately home in Oxfordshire, birthplace of Churchill
a red-and-white variety of the King Charles toy spaniel
a Bristol light bomber aircraft that flew in the Second World War

explanation.surface: A grand house, a dog and a wartime aircraft.
explanation.definitionFit: The name belongs to Churchill's ancestral palace, a breed of toy spaniel and a British wartime bomber.

clue.text: Top-class bird moving tail in African capital

indicators.note: moving tail says the last letter is shifted to another place

parts.note: A1 means first-rate, written here with I for the 1
the robin is a bird

explanation.surface: A fine bird flicks its tail in an African city.
explanation.walkthrough: AIROBIN has its final N moved to the front.
explanation.definitionFit: Nairobi is the capital city of Kenya, in East Africa.

clue.text: Distant sound in the country

indicators.note: sound says the word is heard spoken rather than spelt

parts.note: a distant manner is chilly or cold

explanation.surface: A faraway noise heard out in the countryside.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sound' looks like a noise, but it signals the homophone.
explanation.definitionFit: Chile is a long, narrow nation on the west coast of South America.

clue.text: State of popular goddess

parts.note: something popular is in
Diana is the Roman goddess of the hunt

explanation.surface: The condition of a well-loved goddess.
explanation.definitionFit: Indiana is a state in the American Midwest.

clue.text: Italian provincial capital is the least important, somewhat

indicators.note: somewhat says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: An Italian town is dismissed as rather insignificant.
explanation.definitionFit: Asti is a city in Piedmont, capital of the province of the same name.

clue.text: Drunken leader embracing lady around village in Derbyshire

indicators.note: embracing says one piece holds the other inside it
Drunken says the letters of the word are staggered into a new order
around says the word is turned back to front

explanation.surface: A tipsy boss hugs a woman in a Peak District village.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Drunken' scrambles the boss to give DARLEE; 'around' turns the woman to YDAL, and 'embracing' lodges that just before the final E.
explanation.definitionFit: Darley Dale is a village in the Derbyshire Dales near Matlock.

clue.text: US prosecutor accepting a small volume in Bangladesh

indicators.note: accepting says the prosecutor takes the other pieces inside

parts.note: DA is a district attorney, an American public prosecutor
cc, cubic centimetre, is a small volume

explanation.surface: An American lawyer takes on a short book in South Asia.
explanation.walkthrough: 'small volume' looks like a slim book, but it is a unit of measure.
explanation.definitionFit: Dacca, now usually Dhaka, is the capital city of Bangladesh.

clue.text: Top actors swapping notes in Yorkshire

indicators.note: swapping notes says one musical letter is exchanged for another

parts.note: the leads are the principal actors in a production

explanation.surface: Star performers exchange messages in a northern English county.
explanation.walkthrough: A and E are both musical notes; LEADS swaps its A for E.
explanation.definitionFit: Leeds is the largest city in West Yorkshire.

clue.text: Talkative bird swallows whale on Mediterranean isle

indicators.note: swallows says the bird takes the whale inside it

parts.note: the mina, or myna, is a bird that mimics speech
an orc is a killer whale

explanation.surface: A chattering bird gulps down a whale on an island.
explanation.definitionFit: Minorca, or Menorca, is one of the Balearic Islands in the western Mediterranean.

clue.text: Unstable wet mass at Cornish resort

indicators.note: Unstable says the letters are wobbled into a new order

explanation.surface: Shifting wet sand at a Cornish beach.
explanation.definitionFit: St Mawes is a seaside village on the Roseland peninsula in Cornwall.

clue.text: City in France — one in Nepal, maybe

indicators.note: in says the numeral goes inside the country name
maybe says the letters could be arranged another way

parts.note: one is I, the Roman numeral

explanation.surface: A French town is compared to somewhere in the Himalayas.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' puts I inside NEPAL and 'maybe' rearranges the result.
explanation.definitionFit: Épinal is a town in the Vosges region of north-eastern France.

clue.text: Secondary thoroughfares for Norfolk waters

definitions.meaning: ... are the minor roads in the British road numbering scheme
the shallow lakes and rivers of the Norfolk and Suffolk wetlands

explanation.surface: Back roads lead to the lakes of East Anglia.
explanation.definitionFit: British minor routes are B roads, and the waterways of eastern England are called the Broads.
